cues.en: Queues really are pretty simple, right? You have a producer that enqueues messages, you have a consumer that de queues messages, typically but not always
cues.zh: 队列其实很简单，对吧？有一个生产者把消息入队，有一个消费者把消息出队，通常但不总是

cues.en: But something that is maybe non obvious is that in addition to the active enqueuing being a side effect, right, we get back just confirmation that was added. Because what we are getting back is not a function of the data,
cues.zh: 但有一点也许不那么明显：主动入队本身是一个副作用，对吧，我们拿回来的只是“已添加”的确认。因为我们拿回来的并不是数据的函数，

cues.zh: 数据本身只能描述一个副作用，对吧？队列是处理动作的一种方式。也正因如此，我觉得在 Clojure 社区里它一直有点边缘，对吧？Java 给我们提供了队列，我们偶尔用用，尽可能对它们做抽象。

cues.en: And so looking under the covers, a CoreAsync channel has not one but three queues. It has a buffer that holds the messages, but it also has a puts queue
cues.zh: 所以往底层看，一个 core.async channel 不是一个队列，而是三个队列。它有一个缓冲区存放消息，但它还有一个 puts 队列，

cues.en: where producers that are trying to add to a full buffer will wait and a takes queue where consumers that are trying to take messages from an empty buffer will wait.
cues.zh: 那些想往满缓冲区里添加的生产者会在这里等待；还有一个 takes 队列，那些想从空缓冲区取消息的消费者会在这里等待。

cues.en: But once we've sort of traversed this, once the producer has successfully handed off a message to the consumer,
cues.zh: 但一旦我们完成了这样的遍历，一旦生产者成功地把消息交给了消费者，

cues.en: that's not the end of the story because the consumer has provided a callback
cues.zh: 这还没完，因为消费者提供了一个回调

cues.en: wherein it says what it wants to do with the message. And that callback has to be run on a thread pool. And a thread pool in Java has another queue that sits between the people who want something,
cues.zh: 在回调里说明它想对消息做什么。而这个回调必须在线程池上运行。而 Java 中的线程池还有另一个队列，位于想要完成某事的人

cues.en: to be done and the queues that can do it. And typically,
cues.zh: 和能完成它的队列之间。通常来说，

cues.en: the size of a thread pool is dynamic, and what causes a thread pool to grow is, trying to add something to the blocking queue and finding that the queue is full, at which point a new thread will be spun up
cues.zh: 线程池的大小是动态的，导致线程池增长的原因是，尝试往阻塞队列里添加东西时发现队列已满，此时就会启动一个新线程

cues.en: unless we have the maximum number of threads, whatever we define that to be, in which case it will throw a rejected execution exception, which is something that we should always be aware of when using a thread pool.
cues.zh: 除非已经达到了最大线程数，无论我们定义的是多少，这种情况下它会抛出拒绝执行异常，这是我们在使用线程池时应该时刻注意的。

cues.en: And the blocking queue under the covers looks a great deal like core async. It has a buffer that holds the messages, and it has these things called conditions or condition queues that are called not full and not empty respectively.
cues.zh: 而阻塞队列在底层看起来非常像 core async。它有一个缓冲区来存放消息，还有一些叫做条件或条件队列的东西，分别叫做 not full 和 not empty。

cues.en: Unlike a typical queue though, it's just a place for threads to park themselves. There's no actual conveyance of information. And so, when a producer comes in and finds a buffer to be full, it will release all the locks and will park itself at the not full condition and wait to be notified that the buffer is not full.
cues.zh: 不过与典型的队列不同，它只是线程停靠的地方。并没有实际的信息传递。所以，当生产者进来发现缓冲区已满时，它会释放所有锁，停在 not full 条件上，等待被通知缓冲区不满。

cues.en: And, when it's notified, only one of the threads that are waiting there will actually, be woken up.
cues.zh: 当收到通知时，在那里等待的线程中，实际上只有一个会被唤醒。

cues.zh: 而条件变量，

cues.zh: 则深埋在 JVM 的实现中。我不太确定它们具体是怎么工作的。但这是线程之间进行某种协作的一种方式。不过，即使是操作系统级别的那些线程，也有另一个用于调度的队列。而且，这些软件线程还得排队等待分配到我们机器的硬件线程或核心上。因此，在我们和我们想让计算机做的所有事情之间，大概有半打左右的队列

cues.zh: 去了解它们。队列之所以如此无处不在，是因为

cues.en: they separate what we want to have happen from when it happens. And this is really valuable because most of the time when we write code, we don't know what else is going on. cues.zh: 由于同样的原因，鉴于它们的无处不在，我们理应理解队列是如何工作的、它们是如何失效的、以及当它们过载时会发生什么。

cues.en: one of the key distinctions in queuing theory is between closed and open systems. A closed system is where, as we produce something, we must wait for the consumer to complete it before
cues.zh: 排队论中一个关键的区分是封闭系统与开放系统。所谓封闭系统，就是当我们生产了某种东西后，必须等消费者处理完毕，然后才能

cues.en: producing something else. And we're all very familiar with an example of this, which is a REPL, right. If it reads in our input, it must evaluate and print the result before looping back. Another example of a closed system is a single person browsing a website. They receive a page, they click on the link and they must wait for the next page to load before they can click again. And so naturally, they are sort of seeding control to each other.
cues.zh: 生产下一个。大家都非常熟悉的一个例子就是 REPL，对吧。它读取我们的输入，必须先求值并打印结果，然后才会进入下一次循环。封闭系统的另一个例子是一个人浏览网页。他们收到页面，点击链接，必须等下一个页面加载完成才能再次点击。所以很自然地，它们就像是在相互交替出让控制权。

cues.zh: 而封闭系统则是

cues.en: But what they look like as they lead up to failure is very different.
cues.zh: 但它们走向失败时的表现却大不相同。

cues.en: And sort of conceptually why this is, is that every time that an expensive task comes in,
cues.zh: 从概念上讲，原因在于：每当一个高开销任务到来时，

cues.en: in the case where you only have one consumer, it's
cues.zh: 在只有一个消费者的情况下，

cues.en: focused entirely on that, right? And things are starting to kind of pile up behind it, right? These long tail tasks, these complex tasks
cues.zh: 它会完全专注在那个任务上，对吧？然后其他东西开始堆积在后面，对吧？这些长尾任务、这些复杂任务

cues.en: completely cripple our ability to keep up. But when you have four consumers, only three out of the four consumers
cues.zh: 彻底削弱了我们跟上的能力。但当你拥有四个消费者时，四个中只有三个

cues.en: can sort of continue, but we still are able to make some forward progress. And likewise with the 16,
cues.zh: 能继续处理，但我们仍然能够取得一些进展。同样地，有 16 个消费者时，

cues.en: we have to have a very unusual confluence of events come in for us to be completely
cues.zh: 必须要有一个非常罕见的事件汇聚，才能让我们完全

cues.en: sort of taken up with these long tail tasks.
cues.zh: 被这些长尾任务占满。

cues.en: But
cues.zh: 但是

cues.en: you'll notice that
cues.zh: 你会注意到

cues.en: in the case of the 16, it looks very, very good, almost up until the point where it falls over. And I will point out that this is the best analog
cues.zh: 在 16 个消费者的情况下，它看起来非常非常好，几乎一直到它崩溃的那一刻。我要指出，这是最能类比

cues.en: for the systems that we build. We have multiple machines. We have multiple threads. And so we can absolutely have a system which is responding in sub millisecond time right up to the point where it becomes completely unstable, right? It happens pretty much all at once.
cues.zh: 我们所构建系统的例子。我们有多台机器，多个线程。所以我们完全可能有一个系统，它一直以亚毫秒级响应，直到它变得完全不稳定，对吧？这几乎是一瞬间发生的。

cues.en: And so what we've learned here is that, your systems are typically open ones or at least the ones that you will struggle to sort of understand as they run-in production.
cues.zh: 所以我们在这里学到的是，你的系统通常是开放系统，或者至少是那些在生产运行中你难以理解其行为的系统。

cues.en: And it's the long tail
cues.zh: 正是你任务的

cues.en: of your tasks that cause your system to kind of fill up, right? And so, we can't just look at what the mean or median complexity. We have to be very aware of what the unusually complex tasks look like and track that very, very closely.
cues.zh: 长尾部分导致系统被填满，对吧？所以我们不能只看均值或中位复杂度。我们必须非常清楚那些异常复杂的任务长什么样，并且非常密切地跟踪它们。

cues.en: And this is important not just because of us looking at the complexity of things that are downstream of us, but also because the
cues.zh: 这不仅重要，是因为我们要看下游事物的复杂度，还因为

cues.en: outliers in our own response time are what will make the systems that are relying upon us stable or unstable.
cues.zh: 我们自身响应时间的异常值，才是决定依赖我们的系统是否稳定的关键。

cues.en: And so using more consumers will reduce our variance right up until the point where the system actually falls over, which is inevitable, right? There is no way that we can protect against this. Data at some point will outstrip our ability if only for a short period of time.
cues.zh: 因此，增加消费者会降低我们的方差，直到系统最终崩溃的那一个临界点——这是不可避免的，对吧？我们没有任何办法来防范这一点。数据量在某些时候一定会超出我们的处理能力，哪怕只是短短的一会儿。

cues.en: And so the real lesson here and the one thing that I hope that you take away from this is that
cues.zh: 所以，这里真正的教训，也是我希望大家能从中记住的一点，那就是

cues.en: unbounded queues are fundamentally broken because it puts the correctness of your system in somebody else's hands, right. You have no control over how fast the data is showing up. And so that means that someone can, intentionally or unintentionally, cause your system to break.
cues.zh: 无界队列从根本上就是坏掉的，因为它把系统的正确性交到了别人手里，对吧。你根本无法控制数据出现的速率。这意味着无论是故意还是无意，总有人能让你的系统崩溃。

cues.en: And so we cannot have our strategy for dealing with too much data to hold onto it and hope for the best. We have to do something a little bit more proactive.
cues.zh: 因此，当我们面对过多数据时，不能采取把数据存起来、祈祷一切顺利的策略。我们必须采取更积极主动的措施。

cues.en: And so
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: when we look at this problem, what happens when too much data shows up, we really have only three strategies. We can drop the data on the floor.
cues.zh: 当我们看待这个问题时——当大量数据涌入时会发生什么——其实我们只有三种策略。我们可以直接丢弃数据。

cues.en: We can reject the data, which is to say drop the data on the floor and let them know that we dropped it. Or we can pause the data, which is to say back to whoever's giving us the data, I can't handle this right now. And then at some point in the future say, now I can.
cues.zh: 我们可以拒绝数据，也就是说，丢弃数据并让对方知道我们丢了。或者我们可以暂停数据流，也就是告诉给我们发数据的人：“我现在处理不过来。”然后在未来的某个时刻再告诉他们：“现在可以了。”

cues.en: And so dropping the data is actually a valid strategy for a certain subset of problems where the newer data makes the older data obsolete. Once we get a new piece of data, we can drop anything else we had before. It doesn't matter anymore. And this would be true for some cases of telemetry,
cues.zh: 所以丢掉数据对于某类特定问题其实是有效策略，也就是新数据会让旧数据过时的情况。一旦拿到新数据，之前的数据就可以全部丢弃，因为它们不再重要了。这在某些遥测场景下确实成立，

cues.en: some sensor systems. It's generally a pretty narrow set of problems.
cues.zh: 比如一些传感器系统。但总体来说，这类问题范围相当窄。

cues.en: The other reason we can drop the data is if we just don't care, if it's sort of best effort, right? We'd like to have the data if we possibly could, but if we don't, then oh well.
cues.zh: 另一个可以丢数据的原因是，我们根本不在乎，也就是尽力而为就行。能拿到数据当然好，但拿不到也就算了。

cues.en: I think that we do this a little bit too readily, honestly.
cues.zh: 说实话，我觉得我们用这个理由用得太随意了。

cues.en: For instance, you can see that monitoring systems like StatsD use UDP, which is, again, a sort of best effort delivery. You fire it and sort of just pray that it gets there.
cues.zh: 比如，像 StatsD 这样的监控系统用的是 UDP，这又是一种尽力而为的投递方式。发出去之后，就只能祈祷它能到达。

cues.en: And you'll see this sort of correlation between
cues.zh: 你会发现存在这样一种相关性：

cues.en: situations where the network is in crisis
cues.zh: 网络处于危机状态的场景

cues.en: and the sort of likeliness of this data being dropped, which means that when we most need accurate data, we're least likely to get it. And so this certainly is a thing that we can do, but we should often, if we can, sort of search for a better approach.
cues.zh: 和这些数据被丢弃的可能性之间，是相关的。也就是说，在我们最需要准确数据的时候，反而最不容易拿到。所以这确实是一种可行的做法，但只要可以，我们往往应该去寻找更好的方案。

cues.en: Rejecting the data is pretty much what you see when you go to an overloaded website and returns a five zero three, or when Twitter back in the day has returned a fail whale, or any of these other sorts of things. This is the most common thing to do at the application level, because when we have too many requests, we don't have enough information to do something more graceful than that. We can't email the customer
cues.zh: 拒绝数据，基本上就是你访问一个过载的网站时看到它返回 503，或者当年 Twitter 返回 fail whale 之类的情况。这是应用层最常见的做法，因为当请求太多时，我们手头的信息不足以做出更优雅的处理。我们没法给客户发邮件

cues.en: saying, oh, well, can't check out your cart now, but we'll let you know once you can. We don't even know who they are. We have no means to figure out who they are.
cues.zh: 说“哦，现在没法结账，但等能结账了我们会通知你”。我们连他们是谁都不知道，也没有办法弄清楚他们是谁。

cues.en: And so this is far from ideal. Ideally, we would never reject anything, especially if someone's going to pay us money for it. But, we need to have an understanding that this is inevitable. We need to understand what we're going to do in this situation and make that as, palatable as we can.
cues.zh: 所以这远非理想情况。理想情况下，我们什么都不该拒绝，尤其是有人愿意为此付钱的时候。但我们需要认识到这是不可避免的。我们需要明白在这种情况下该怎么做，并尽可能让它变得容易接受。

cues.en: But
cues.zh: 但是

cues.en: elsewhere, right, except when we're not sort of writing code at the application level, when we're trying to write a more general sort of thing,
cues.zh: 在其他地方，对吧，除非我们不是在应用层写代码，而是在写更通用的东西，

cues.en: what we want to do is we want to pause the data or exert back pressure.
cues.zh: 我们想做的就是暂停数据或施加背压。

cues.en: And a closed system, and this is sort of implicit, right? We have this sort of seeding of control between the producer and the consumer and that's sort of built into it. But when we're writing a library or a framework or something like that, we don't know what is appropriate. We don't know if dropping data is appropriate. We don't know how to reject the data in a meaningful way. And so the best thing that we can do is just sort of defer the choice to someone who's upstream and understands the application better than we do.
cues.zh: 在一个封闭系统中，这是隐含的，对吧？生产者和消费者之间有这种控制权的分配，这是内建的。但当我们写库或框架之类的东西时，我们不知道什么是合适的。我们不知道丢弃数据是否合适。我们不知道如何以有意义的方式拒绝数据。所以我们能做的最好的事情就是把选择权交给上游的人，他们比我们更了解应用。

cues.en: And so this is why CoreAsync has
cues.zh: 这就是为什么CoreAsync有

cues.en: three queues instead of just one. It has the puts buffer
cues.zh: 三个队列而不是只有一个。它有puts缓冲区

cues.en: for things which have had back pressure exerted on them, where we've told them we're working on it but we can't quite get to you. And then we'll eventually be able to notify them, it's okay, we took it, you can continue.
cues.zh: 用于那些已经施加了背压的东西，我们已经告诉它们我们正在处理，但暂时还轮不到你。然后我们最终能通知它们，没问题，我们接收了，你可以继续了。

cues.en: And so when we look at queues,
cues.zh: 所以当我们看队列时，

cues.en: as I said, they sort of separate the what from the when. They also sort of allow us to deal with potentially unbounded demand using very bounded resources.
cues.zh: 正如我所说，它们有点像是将“做什么”与“何时做”分离开来。它们还允许我们用非常有限的资源来处理可能无限的需求。

cues.en: And they serve as sort of interface between systems where the demand and the supply may be sort of mismatched or we can't really predict what the relative proportion of each will be. And these are all sort of saying the same thing.
cues.zh: 它们可以充当系统之间的某种接口，在这些系统中，供需可能会有些不匹配，或者我们无法真正预测各自的相对比例。这些其实都在表达同一件事。

cues.en: But the crucial point I want to make is that the buffer, right, the thing that holds onto the messages is unnecessary for any of these properties, right. In fact, we could just as easily have
cues.zh: 但我想强调的关键一点是，缓冲区，也就是保存消息的那个东西，对于上述任何特性来说都不是必需的。事实上，我们完全可以轻松拥有

cues.en: a
cues.zh: 一个

cues.en: channel which has just the puts and the takes, just waits to pass the message off once it's available. And in fact, in QuerySync, this is the default channel configuration. It has no buffer.
cues.zh: 只有放入（puts）和取出（takes）操作的通道，它只是在消息可用时等待将其传递出去。事实上，在 QuerySync 中，这就是默认的通道配置。它没有缓冲区。

cues.en: And the reason that this is good is because an unbuffered queue is a closed system, right? There is that sort of implicit seating of control. We only proceed when someone else has actually taken it off our hands.
cues.zh: 这样做的好处是，无缓冲队列是一个封闭的系统，对吧？这里有一种隐式的控制权交接。只有当别人真正把东西从我们手里接过去时，我们才会继续。

cues.en: And so you may wonder why on earth would we even have buffers? Buffers seem only to be a thing that introduced latency.
cues.zh: 所以你可能会纳闷，我们到底为什么还要用缓冲区？缓冲区似乎只会引入延迟。

cues.en: And the answer to this is that back pressure, right, enacting back pressure and retracking back pressure is not free.
cues.zh: 而答案是，背压（back pressure），也就是施加背压和追踪背压并不是没有代价的。

cues.en: If we want to restart a thread that we stopped, we have to copy the stack back into memory. If we want to restart TCP traffic that stopped, we have to send a message over the network and wait for the rate of traffic to ramp back up. If we're reading off the disk or database, we have to go and actually do that. And the time that elapses between us saying we're ready and someone actually giving us something to work on is
cues.zh: 如果我们想重启一个暂停的线程，我们就必须把栈复制回内存中。如果我们想恢复暂停的 TCP 流量，我们就必须通过网络发送消息，并等待流量速率重新爬升。如果我们正在从磁盘或数据库读取数据，我们就必须亲自去执行这些操作。从我们说“我们准备好了”到别人真正给我们可处理的工作之间流逝的时间，

cues.en: hurting our overall throughput, our actual rate of handling the data.
cues.zh: 会损害我们的整体吞吐量，也就是我们处理数据的实际速率。

cues.en: And so that's what buffers are good for. Buffers allow us to make sure that our throughput is more stable
cues.zh: 这就是缓冲区的作用所在。缓冲区能够确保我们的吞吐量更加稳定，

cues.en: and as going at just a higher rate. And that's of course at the expense of latency in our systems.
cues.zh: 并且以更高的速率运行。当然，这是以牺牲系统延迟为代价的。

cues.en: And so, we should always plan for too much data. This is something that is inevitable and we need to know what our sort of response to this will be. And wherever possible, we should use back pressure because that's the most neutral choice that we can make, right? That just kind of tells someone else, I can't handle this data, you figure out what that means. And that might sort of flow up on a chain all the way to the periphery of our application before
cues.zh: 因此，我们应该始终为数据过量的情况做好准备。这是不可避免的，我们需要知道对此应采取何种应对方式。在可能的情况下，我们应该使用背压，因为这是我们能做出的最中立的选择，对吧？这只是在告诉别人，我处理不了这些数据，你自己看着办吧。这种信号可能会沿着调用链一层层向上传递，直到到达我们应用程序的边缘，

cues.en: something says, oh, I guess I have to reject or I have to drop or I have to do whatever is appropriate in this situation. But that logic should be centralized. It should not be sort of sprinkled throughout.
cues.zh: 然后某个组件会说，哦，看来我得拒绝、丢弃或者根据当前情况采取适当的措施。但这种逻辑应该是集中的，不应该散落得到处都是。

cues.en: And buffers are useful in that they give us this sort of constant throughput. But it's at the expense of latency and so we should only use them where absolutely necessary. And we should, in practice,
cues.zh: 缓冲区之所以有用，是因为它们能提供这种恒定的吞吐量。但这以延迟为代价，所以我们应该只在绝对必要时使用它们。而且在实践中，

cues.en: avoid composing buffered queues wherever possible because each additional buffer tends to sort of magnify the results of the next.
cues.zh: 我们应该尽可能避免组合多个缓冲队列，因为每增加一个缓冲区，往往都会放大下一个缓冲区带来的影响。

cues.en: And so
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: as we've been going through this, we've had some things that, we've decided or I've told you and,
cues.zh: 在我们探讨这些内容的过程中，有一些事情是我们已经确定的，或者是我告诉过大家的，

cues.en: it's worth taking a moment to sort of compare these guidelines to the current state of the Clojure ecosystem.
cues.zh: 我们不妨花点时间，将这些准则与 Clojure 生态系统的现状做个对比。

cues.en: A lot of the attempts to kind of take something like QuerySync, which absolutely sort of, it implements back pressure and everything flawlessly.
cues.zh: 很多尝试都是拿 QuerySync 这类东西来用，它确实能完美实现背压等等。

cues.en: But then it is hooked up to some sort of networking mechanism, right? Something where, again, we have no control over how much data is coming in
cues.zh: 但随后它又被接到某种网络机制上，对吧？这种机制同样让我们无法控制有多少数据进来。

cues.en: and it doesn't hook it up properly.
cues.zh: 而且它没有正确地把两者接起来。

cues.en: And in some cases, is unavoidable. For instance, the Java EE spec for WebSockets has no mechanism for backpressure. I don't know why, but it doesn't.
cues.zh: 在某些情况下，这是不可避免的。比如 Java EE 的 WebSockets 规范就没有背压机制。我不知道为什么，但确实没有。

cues.en: And so,
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: when you are trying to use this in a server container or something like that, there's no real way to solve this problem. But in other cases, it's just sort of an oversight, right? This particular author has never been bit by this problem, doesn't see sort of how important it is to make these sorts of connections, not break the golden chain of back pressure.
cues.zh: 当你试图在服务器容器之类的地方使用它时，这个问题其实没法真正解决。但在其他情况下，这不过是疏忽，对吧？这位作者从没被这个问题坑过，也看不出建立这类连接、不破坏背压这条黄金链有多重要。

cues.en: And so we as consumers of libraries, I think, need to be more discerning. We need to ask the tough questions when we look at this sort of stuff and make sure that we're not building on top of shaky foundations.
cues.zh: 所以我认为，作为库的使用者，我们需要更有辨别力。看这类东西时，要问那些尖锐的问题，确保我们不是建在摇摇欲坠的地基上。

cues.en: And this is not to call out any of the authors who have made a library, many of which are
cues.zh: 这不是要指责任何编写库的作者，其中很多库

cues.en: used to good effect within our community.
cues.zh: 在我们的社区里用得很好。

cues.en: But I think that we want to make sure that our ecosystem
cues.zh: 但我认为，我们希望确保我们的生态系统

cues.en: can stand up to any scale of system, right? That we are not forced to rebuild from scratch once we hit the point of failure, which can happen just all of a sudden, right?
cues.zh: 能够支撑任意规模的系统，对吧？确保我们不会一旦遇到故障点就被迫从头重建，而故障可能突然就发生，对吧？

cues.en: And so a concrete example of this
cues.zh: 这就是一个具体的例子

cues.en: is an open system that I work on which is called MAW.
cues.zh: 是我参与开发的一个开放系统，叫MAW。

cues.en: And MAW is sort of this omnivorous
cues.zh: MAW 有点像这种杂食性的

cues.en: endpoint that just absorbs any data that our partners or customers send to us.
cues.zh: 端点，能吸收合作伙伴或客户发给我们的任何数据。

cues.en: And so the general idea looks something like this. We have a large amount of data coming in. We need to do a little bit of processing to it, and then we need to persist it somewhere for batch processing in the future.
cues.zh: 整体思路大概是这样。我们有大量数据涌入，需要做一点处理，然后保存到某个地方，供以后批量处理。

cues.en: And because I didn't want to have to work very hard on the hard parts of this,
cues.zh: 因为我不想在那些难搞的部分上费太多力气，

cues.en: I decided to do this on AWS, which gives us the Elastic Load Balancer, which is a place you can sort of point arbitrary amounts of traffic and have it spread it across a bunch of machines.
cues.zh: 我决定把它放在AWS上，这样就有弹性负载均衡器，你可以把任意量的流量指向它，让它分发到一堆机器上。

cues.en: And I wanted to persist to S3,
cues.zh: 我还想持久化到S3，

cues.en: which is a replicated data store which is
cues.zh: 这是一个可复制的数据存储，

cues.en: highly available and is able to kind of deal with whatever volumes of data that we want to write to it.
cues.zh: 高可用，能应付我们想写入的任何数据量。

cues.en: And the system has some pretty,
cues.zh: 这个系统有一些相当

cues.en: particular properties, right. It has to be horizontally scalable because we don't know,
cues.zh: 特殊的性质。它必须能横向扩展，因为我们不知道

cues.en: how many how much data we're going to need, right. When it first, was started up, we were getting about 40,000 queries per second. We're up to about 300,000
cues.zh: 需要多少数据。刚启动时，我们每秒大约有4万次查询，一年半后峰值到了大约30万

cues.en: at peak, about a year and a half later. And so,
cues.zh: 次。所以，

cues.en: I wanted to be able to have that just kind of work without me having to go back and sort of rethink the entire thing. And it must be low maintenance. This is far from the only thing that I am responsible for. If it takes up more than a day out of a month of my time, then something's gone horribly wrong.
cues.zh: 我希望它能自动应对，而不用我回过头重新设计整个系统。而且它必须维护成本低。这远不是我唯一负责的事。如果它每月占用我超过一天时间，那就出大问题了。

cues.en: It's not real time. We don't really care about the data getting into S3 in any particular,
cues.zh: 这不是实时的。我们并不太在意数据以多快的速度写入 S3，

cues.en: rapid pace as long as it's sort of there by the end of the day.
cues.zh: 只要它能在一天结束前差不多都存进去就行。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: the most important property is that the loss of the data is more or less directly proportional to loss of utility. If we lose 1% of the data, we lose about 1% of the utility. And this is very different than if we were doing say payment processing, where losing 1% of the data would make us useless,
cues.zh: 最重要的特性是，数据的丢失与实用性的损失大致呈正比。如果我们丢失了 1% 的数据，我们也就损失了大约 1% 的实用性。这跟我们处理支付之类的情况非常不同，那种情况下丢失 1% 的数据就会让我们彻底瘫痪，

cues.en: right. And so this is a very particular property which makes my job a lot easier.
cues.zh: 对吧。所以这是一个非常特殊的属性，让我的工作轻松了很多。

cues.en: And so,
cues.zh: 因此，

cues.en: sort of previously we had set up a system that absorbed the Twitter garden hose, which is 10 of the Twitter fire hose.
cues.zh: 之前我们搭建了一个系统，用来接收 Twitter 园艺软管（Twitter garden hose）的数据，这相当于 Twitter 火力全开数据流（fire hose）的十分之一。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: this is the official term.
cues.zh: 这是官方术语。

And so I had kind of jammed something together, which took an HTTP client stream and then put it through the Hadoop S3 client, which was something that we had on hand and wrote it to S3. And this worked very well. And so in my sort of initial, let's just get something up and running, I adapted that and put a web server in front of it and then wrote the entries, which I assumed to be about 20,000 entries per second
cues.zh: 最终这大约是每秒 600 条推文。所以我当时拼凑了一个东西，它接收一个 HTTP 客户端流，然后通过 Hadoop S3 客户端（这是我们手头现成的工具）将其写入 S3。这运行得非常好。所以在我的初步构想中——也就是先搞个能跑起来的系统，我改造了那个程序，在前面加了一个 Web 服务器，然后把这些条目（我估计大约是每秒 20,000 条）

cues.en: through the Hadoop client.
cues.zh: 通过 Hadoop 客户端写入。

cues.en: But
cues.zh: 但是

cues.en: what I was unaware of, what I had not really been tracking with the Twitter client was that occasionally
cues.zh: 我没有意识到、也没有真正关注 Twitter 客户端的一点是，S3 偶尔会

cues.en: S3 becomes
cues.zh: 变得

cues.en: unavailable,
cues.zh: 不可用，

cues.en: right. For whatever reason, I still don't really know why, but it just stops accepting rights for a bit.
cues.zh: 对吧。不管出于什么原因，我其实到现在也不知道为什么，但它就是会有一段时间停止接收写入。

cues.en: And what happens in this case is that the Hadoop S3 client sort of just held on to everything, hoping that eventually everything would sort of work itself out and be able to flush all the accumulated data. But in fact, it was getting stuff at too rapid a pace, and so we ran out of memory and the system fell over. And then all of the traffic that that machine was handling fell over to the other machines, which themselves fell over, and then the entire system was dead.
cues.zh: 在这种情况下，Hadoop S3客户端只是把所有数据都攥着不放，希望最终一切都能自行解决，把累积的数据全部刷出去。但实际上，数据涌入的速度太快，结果我们内存耗尽，系统崩溃了。然后那台机器处理的所有流量都转移到了其他机器上，那些机器也接连崩溃，最终整个系统瘫痪了。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: to be clear, this was almost certainly happening with the Twitter client before because,
cues.zh: 说清楚一点，这种情况几乎肯定之前在Twitter客户端上也发生过，因为

cues.en: I
cues.zh: 我

cues.en: don't see why they would behave any differently. And in fact, I'm sure that many times it held onto the data and was able to flush it out, right? This was sort of invisible to me. This was not a failure mode I was thinking very carefully about,
cues.zh: 想不出它们的行为会有什么不同。事实上，我确信有很多次它攥住了数据，并且成功刷了出去，对吧？这对我来说几乎是无形的。这不是我认真思考过的故障模式，

cues.en: until I saw it and had to deal with it.
cues.zh: 直到我亲眼看到它并不得不处理它。

cues.en: And so,
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: when I sort of thought about this a little bit more clearly though, I realized that I was making my job a lot harder than it had to be because I was treating the handling of this data as getting it all the way into S3, right, which again is sort of over a network hop, requires it to be replicated and everything else. And really all I wanted was for it to be somewhere that was not in memory.
cues.zh: 不过，当我稍微更清晰地思考这个问题时，我意识到我让自己的工作比实际上要难得多，因为我把处理这些数据当成了要一路送进S3，对吧，这又得经过网络跳转，需要复制等等。而实际上我想要的只是把它放到某个不在内存里的地方。

cues.en: I could write it to the local disk, for instance, which is much more highly available, as it turns out, than S3.
cues.zh: 比如，我可以把它写到本地磁盘上，事实证明，本地磁盘的可用性比S3高得多。

cues.en: And obviously this has some shortcomings, right?
cues.zh: 显然，这存在一些缺点，对吧？

cues.en: In this case, if we lose the machine, we lose the data. But again, this is something that for this particular use case I was okay with.
cues.zh: 在这种情况下，机器一旦故障，数据就会丢失。但同样，对于这个特定场景，我是可以接受这一点的。

cues.en: And so
cues.zh: 于是

cues.en: I ended up writing two libraries, both of which are open source.
cues.zh: 我最终写了两个库，而且全都开源了。

cues.en: One of which is called Durable Queue, is exactly what it sounds like. It's a disk backed queue.
cues.zh: 其中一个叫 Durable Queue，顾名思义，它是一个基于磁盘持久化的队列。

cues.en: Very simple, very
cues.zh: 非常简单，而且

cues.en: sort of well tested. It's had about, I think at this point, three to 4,000,000,000,000 events flowing through it.
cues.zh: 经过了充分测试。到目前为止，流经它的事件大概有三到四万亿条了。

cues.en: And then likewise, S3 journal, is built on top of the durable queue, right. It will write each of the things it intends to upload to S3 to disk. And then on the other side have a consumer which is uploading it as a table.
cues.zh: 同样，S3 journal 是构建在 Durable Queue 之上的。它会把打算上传到 S3 的内容先写入磁盘，然后在另一端由一个消费者负责将其作为表上传。

cues.en: And so the system that I end up building looks like this, right. And so now there are actually two stages. The HTTP server is only concerned with the act of getting it onto some persisted store.
cues.zh: 我最终构建的系统就是这样的。现在它实际上分成了两个阶段：HTTP server 只负责把数据写入某种持久化存储。

cues.en: And then there is a different sort of producer and consumer, a different loop, which is uploading that to S3.
cues.zh: 然后由另一组生产者和消费者、也就是另一个循环，负责将其上传到 S3。

cues.en: And of course, the fact that I've simply made my job easier doesn't mean that it's always going to work. And so I need to make sure that everything is working. And so one of the flaws arguably of the Hadoop S3 client wasn't that it just had an unbounded queue. It's that it was invisible, right? We don't know what's going on inside of it. We only know by inferring
cues.zh: 当然，把工作变简单并不意味着它就总能正常运行，我必须确保一切运转良好。可以说，Hadoop S3 client 的缺陷之一不仅仅是它有一个无界队列，更在于它是黑盒不可见的，对吧？我们不知道内部发生了什么，只能事后推断——

cues.en: that once our system fails it was because our memory has sort of ballooned out of control.
cues.zh: 一旦系统崩溃，就是因为内存失控暴涨了。

cues.en: And so S3 journal and the underlying queue both have metrics.
cues.zh: S3 journal和底层队列都有指标。

cues.en: You can go and poll it and say, what is your status? In this case, how many things have I enqueued to you and how much have you successfully uploaded?
cues.zh: 你可以去轮询它，问，你的状态如何？在这种情况下，我已经向你入队了多少东西，你成功上传了多少？

cues.en: And the queue underneath has even more stuff, says how many slabs, which are the files that it's writing to, do you have currently resident in memory? How many things are pending? How many things have you had to retry?
cues.zh: 底层的队列还有更多信息，比如有多少slab，也就是它正在写入的文件，当前有多少驻留在内存中？有多少东西待处理？有多少东西不得不重试？

cues.en: And so this is crucial. This allows us to say what is the health of our system. It allows us to quantify how much we might have lost when a machine goes down. These are all things that are absolutely critical because we cannot prove
cues.zh: 所以这很关键。这让我们能够说明系统的健康状况。它让我们能够量化当一台机器宕机时我们可能损失了多少。这些都是绝对关键的事情，因为我们无法证明

cues.en: properties about our system, right? The system is too complicated. We can only look and see what happens
cues.zh: 关于我们系统的性质，对吧？系统太复杂了。我们只能观察并看看会发生什么

cues.en: in as much as the metrics that we have created for ourselves allow us to do that.
cues.zh: 在我们为自己创建的指标允许我们这样做的范围内。

cues.en: But on the far side of this, on the HTTP intake side,
cues.zh: 但在这的另一边，在HTTP接收侧，

cues.en: there is the additional problem that we need to respond to everyone who's sending us data quickly. Tell them, yes, we've accepted your data. Because otherwise they will scale back the volume of data that we're sending us. And we're trying to get everything that we possibly can.
cues.zh: 还有一个额外的问题，我们需要快速响应每个向我们发送数据的人。告诉他们，是的，我们已经接受了你的数据。因为否则他们会缩减发送给我们的数据量。而我们正试图尽可能获取一切。

cues.en: And so,
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: underneath the Aleph HP server, it uses Neti. And Neti has a very particular threading model where every time a connection is opened, it's assigned to a thread.
cues.zh: 在Aleph HP服务器下面，它使用了Neti。而Neti有一个非常特定的线程模型，每次打开连接时，它都会被分配到一个线程。

cues.en: And many connections are assigned to a given thread, which means that if any,
cues.zh: 许多连接会被分配给同一个线程，这意味着只要有任何连接

cues.en: connection takes up that thread, right, blocks on it or something, that implicitly
cues.zh: 连接会占用那个线程，对吧？会在上面阻塞之类的，这会隐式地…

cues.en: blocks a bunch of other connections that didn't really want to be included in that decision.
cues.zh: 阻碍了一堆本来并不想参与这个决定的其他连接。

cues.en: And so the way that you deal with this is that you put another thread pool behind it, right, that sort of goes and spreads this out and makes sure that no one connection acting
cues.zh: 应对办法是在它后面再加一个线程池，把负载分散开，确保没有哪个连接的行为

cues.en: badly can cause other things to back up.
cues.zh: 处理不当会导致其他任务积压。

cues.zh: 当我们查看这里的指标时，

There's a queue, we spend some time on it and then it happens eventually, who knows when.
cues.zh: 如果在 ring handler 里加了监控来观察响应时间，它其实和真实的响应时间相差甚远，也就是数据包从进入到离开的真正耗时。这是因为线程池本身并没有被很好地做埋点监控，对吧。它们就像是隐形的一样。有个队列，任务在里面耗上一阵，然后不知何时才终于被执行。

cues.en: And so there's a library that I wrote which
cues.zh: 所以我写了一个库，它

cues.en: has a bunch of stuff, in it, but one of them is an instrumented thread pool, right, something that actually tracks all the relative statistics. And so when I go,
cues.zh: 里面有很多东西，但其中之一是经过插桩的线程池，对吧，它能实际追踪所有相关统计数据。所以当我

cues.zh: 对于任何正在运行的 MAW 服务器，都有一个类似这样的 JSON 端点。我要重点关注的是，

cues.en: two aspects of this.
cues.zh: 这有两个方面。

cues.en: One of which is the,
cues.zh: 其中之一是，

cues.en: sort of measuring the task rejection, completion, and arrival rate. And notice that none of these are just simple scalar values. They're all quantiles.
cues.zh: 差不多就是测量任务的拒绝率、完成率和到达率。而且注意，这些都不是简单的标量值。它们全都是分位数。

cues.en: Because, again, the rate of arrival is going to be sort of spiking and going down as sort of different
cues.zh: 因为，同样的，请求到达的速率会有所波动，时高时低，

cues.zh: 因为那些互不协调的请求有时会同时涌现，有时又全无踪影。因此你会发现，在到达率和完成率之间，中位数和 99.9 分位数之间大约有三倍的差距。

cues.en: And so when you talk about capacity planning, right, we have to think about that. Likewise, we are in fact sometimes rejecting
cues.zh: 所以当谈到容量规划时，对吧，我们必须考虑到这一点。同样地，我们事实上有时会

cues.zh: 拒绝数据，因为我们没有足够的容量来处理。这种情况似乎发生得非常少。

cues.en: But this is something that we should absolutely be tracking.
cues.zh: 但这是我们绝对应该追踪的事情。

cues.en: There's also the task latency and the queue latency, where the task latency is a superset. It represents the entire time spent on the queue and working on the task. And the queue latency represents just the time spent on the queue. You'll notice that the 99.9 percentile for the queue is actually higher than that for the task, that's because these are sampled
cues.zh: 这里还有任务延迟和队列延迟，其中任务延迟是一个超集。它代表在队列上以及处理任务所花费的总时间。而队列延迟仅代表在队列中花费的时间。你会发现队列的 99.9 分位数实际上比任务的还要高，这是因为这些是抽样

cues.en: statistics.
cues.zh: 统计数据。

cues.en: Sometimes
cues.zh: 有时候

cues.zh: 队列所观察到的和任务所观察到的会略有不同。所以这是不完美的。它并不是我们系统的高保真完美视图，但它已经足够好了。

cues.en: And you'll also notice that the queue is zero in length all the time because it is actually an unbuffered queue. And yet somehow we're spending two milliseconds sometimes trying to traverse it. And this is because of course, underneath our queue, which is unbuffered, there are many queues which are buffered, right? All the things that sit underneath the execution model of Java. And so again, we need to measure that. We need to be aware of these things and not just treat this as some sort of instantaneous process of handing off between producer and consumer.
cues.zh: 你还会发现队列的长度一直为零，因为它实际上是一个无缓冲队列。然而有时我们却要花两毫秒的时间来穿过它。这当然是因为，在我们这个无缓冲的队列底层，其实有很多有缓冲的队列，对吧？也就是 Java 执行模型底层的所有那些东西。所以同样地，我们需要对这些进行测量。我们需要意识到这些事情，而不能仅仅把它当作生产者和消费者之间某种即时交接的过程。

cues.en: And so we have metrics now, right? We have
cues.zh: 所以我们现在有了指标，对吧？我们有

cues.en: something that gives us a little bit more visibility in the system. It obviously doesn't actually capture everything. It doesn't look very deep into METI. And if we ever saw a huge discrepancy between the response times that we were seeing and the response times being reported outside of our system, we would have to dig into that, right. There's always something more to measure. But the idea is that we just don't want to be sort of willfully blind and close our eyes and pretend that everything's okay.
cues.zh: 能让我们对系统有更多可见性的东西。显然，它并不能真正捕获所有东西。它对 METI 的观察不够深入。如果我们发现我们看到的响应时间和系统外部报告的响应时间之间存在巨大差异，我们就必须深入研究，对吧。总会有更多东西需要测量。但我们的想法是，我们不想盲目乐观、闭上眼睛假装一切都好。

cues.en: And so
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: it's really crucial when we're building these systems that we understand what it means to complete something, right, because too many things that are incomplete means that we need to apply back pressure or drop data or reject it. And so if we can sort of move the goalpost and make that easier,
cues.zh: 在构建这些系统时，理解完成某事的含义至关重要，对吧，因为有太多未完成的事情意味着我们需要施加背压、丢弃数据或拒绝它。因此，如果我们能稍微移动球门并使其变得更容易，

cues.en: that is a huge win.
cues.zh: 那将是一个巨大的胜利。

cues.en: And you should be picky about your tools. You should make sure that they don't sort of subvert your assumptions of what should be happening or
cues.zh: 你应该对工具挑剔一点。你必须确保它们不会颠覆你对应该发生的事情的假设，或者

cues.en: what needs to happen in these sorts of systems.
cues.zh: 这些系统中需要发生的事情。

cues.en: And when choosing a tool, raw performance is good. These benchmarks, they tell us something which is probably if I use this right, it will be fast. But you should always prefer something which actually tells you how fast it is because the assumptions that are from these sorts of very contrived benchmarks will not necessarily
cues.zh: 在选择工具时，原始性能固然很好。这些基准测试告诉我们一些信息：如果我正确使用它，它可能会很快。但你总是应该选择那些真正告诉你它有多快的工具，因为这些非常刻意的基准测试所产生的假设，未必能

cues.en: make their way into reality.
cues.zh: 在现实中实现。

cues.en: And you're never going to be able to measure all of your system. There are always going to be things that are outside of your control. Someone who's accessing your website from a mobile connection, right, might go into a tunnel and lose their connection for x number of seconds.
cues.zh: 而且你永远无法测完你的整个系统。总有一些事情是超出你控制的。比如有人通过移动网络访问你的网站，可能会进隧道然后断网好几秒。

cues.en: And that's clearly not something that you can
cues.zh: 这显然不是你能

cues.en: account for, that you can sort of prevent.
cues.zh: 预料到或去设法阻止的。

cues.en: But that is what they're perceiving your response time to be. And And whether or not that matters, whether or not that's something that you're trying to kind of deal with is very dependent on your application. But there are always going to be things that you are unaware of.
cues.zh: 但这就是他们所感受到的你的响应时间。至于这重不重要，或者是不是你需要去处理的问题，这很大程度上取决于你的应用。不过总会有一些你所不知道的事情发生。

cues.en: And when we have a chat handler, when we actually get some connecting, we, find out what room they want to join.

cues.zh: 然后我们获取该连接的每条消息，并发布到他们选定的房间里，对吧。非常直观，我们只是把所有东西导入另一个流中。

cues.zh: 同样地，我们连上房间，获取房间里的所有发言，再管道传输回该连接。这就是一个聊天处理器，对吧？这就是

cues.zh: 对吧？但这其中存在一些问题。

cues.en: One of which is that if any of our consumers, anybody on the chat
cues.zh: 其中之一是，如果我们的任何消费者，也就是聊天室里的

cues.en: room is slow to receive a message,
cues.zh: 任何人接收消息变慢，

cues.en: that slows down everybody because the act of publishing means it has to go to everyone.
cues.zh: 就会拖慢所有人，因为发布操作意味着必须发送给每个人。

cues.en: And so,
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: we want to
cues.zh: 我们希望

cues.en: sort of control this. We want to make sure that one bad actor doesn't make the entire system sort of destabilize.
cues.zh: 能对此加以控制。我们想确保单个不良节点不会导致整个系统失稳。

cues.en: And so when we're looking at,
cues.zh: 因此，当我们审视

cues.en: this connection, taking
cues.zh: 这个连接时——它负责从房间获取

cues.en: client, whoever they are,
cues.zh: 这个客户端，不论对方是谁——

cues.en: maybe we want to add a buffer, right, be able to write out a few of these sorts of
cues.zh: 也许我们会想加个缓冲区，对吧，来平抑这类

cues.en: instabilities here. Maybe if they are just a little bit slow, we can make it so that that's not too visible to everybody else.
cues.zh: 不稳定性。也许当他们只是稍慢一点时，我们可以让其他所有人基本察觉不到。

cues.en: And of course, measuring this in messages may not be the right thing because who knows how big a message is? It might be one word, it might be a novel. And so a better thing would be to have some sort of metric, right, something that tells us how big the message is and then put an upper bound on the aggregate size of all the messages, in this case just 1,000.
cues.zh: 当然，用消息数量来衡量可能并不对，因为谁知道一条消息有多大呢？它可能是一个词，也可能是一部小说。所以更好的做法是采用某种指标，对吧，能告诉我们消息有多大，然后为所有消息的总大小设置一个上限，这里就是 1000。

cues.en: But even that doesn't necessarily prevent us from arriving at the same failure
cues.zh: 但即便如此，也未必能阻止我们陷入同样的失效

cues.en: mode, right? It just defers it, puts it off a little bit further into the future. And so the only thing that we really can do is once someone is slow to receive our messages, is unable to receive them, we kick them out. And so the connect,
cues.zh: 模式，对吧？它只是延缓了问题，把它推迟到更远的未来。所以我们真正能做的唯一事情，就是一旦有人接收我们的消息变慢了，无法接收它们了，我们就把他们踢出去。所以这里的 connect

cues.en: method here takes a message source
cues.zh: 方法接收一个消息源

cues.en: and pipes all of it, the messages from it into a message sync.
cues.zh: 并将其中的所有消息管道式传输到一个消息接收器中。

cues.en: And there's an optional thing here to define a timeout which says, if I've been trying to give you a message for x
cues.zh: 这里还有一个可选的参数来定义超时，意思是，如果我尝试给你发送消息已经持续了 x

cues.zh: 而我做不到，我就直接关闭你连接，对这事撒手不管了。

cues.en: And so in this case we say, if we've been trying for ten seconds to send you a message and you haven't received it yet, your buffer has been full for that entire time, we're done, you're gone, you can just reconnect.
cues.zh: 所以在这种情况下我们说，如果我们尝试了十秒钟要给你发送消息而你还没收到，你的缓冲区在这期间一直是满的，我们就结束了，你被淘汰了，你可以重新连接。

cues.en: And this is really, again, the only thing we can do. There is no other thing that we can do to save this person from themselves.
cues.zh: 再次强调，这确实是我们唯一能做的事。没有其他办法能把这个人从他们自己造成的困境中拯救出来了。

cues.en: But this actually,
cues.zh: 但这其实，

cues.zh: 这又带来另一个问题：如果有人发布消息太快，就会把所有人压垮，导致大家全被踢出去，

cues.en: right?
cues.zh: 对的，没问题。

cues.zh: 而这可能因为某人是个混蛋，也可能因为某人有点天真。这或许是因为有人就是个混蛋，也可能是因为有人有点天真。

cues.zh: 但这，我是说，这……

所以你真的需要仔细考虑这一点。

cues.zh: 我们

cues.en: And note here that we don't actually need to have the same sort of disconnect logic. Because if someone is sending us messages too rapidly, we'll just keep on using TCP backpressure and saying, nope, we're not taking it. And if that causes them to fail, that's their problem.
cues.zh: 注意，这里我们其实并不需要那种断开连接的逻辑。因为如果有人发消息太快，我们直接用 TCP 背压回应：不，我们接不下了。要是这导致他们出故障，那是他们自己的问题。

cues.en: But in this case, throttling at one message a second may seem a little bit,
cues.zh: 但在这种情况下，把速率限制在每秒一条消息可能会显得有点，

cues.en: irritating because maybe
cues.zh: 很烦人，因为也许

要是有人沉默了十分钟，会发生什么呢？

cues.en: I mean these are sort of both possibilities when we talk about throttling.

cues.zh: 所以我们这里能够指定，

cues.zh: 他们最多能累积的额度。在这个例子中，是十秒的量，对吧。他们可以，如果沉默十秒，就能一次性发10条消息，但不能发更多。

cues.zh: 而

cues.zh: 所以当我们看这个例子时，对吧，它稍微没那么，

We've had to decide what is the maximum amount of memory that we're willing to give to each of these people. How long are we willing to wait on them? How much, how many messages can people send us, right? And so all of a sudden we've gone from this thing which was a little bit hand wavy, a little bit vague, very general. Everybody could sort of project their particular chat room onto it. And now this is a very precise
cues.zh: 像之前那样理想化了，对吧。它稍微没那么通用，因为我们不得不做所有这些决定。我们得决定愿意给每个人多少内存。愿意等他们多久？人们能给我们发多少条消息，对吧？于是突然间，我们从那个有点含糊、有点模糊、非常通用的东西——每个人都能把自己特定的聊天室投射上去——变成了一个非常精确的

cues.en: chat room, right? Maybe not a very good one, but it's certainly precise in terms of what it does.
cues.zh: 聊天室，对吧？也许不是很好的一个，但它在功能上确实是精确的。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而

cues.en: this is what you need to do, right? These are the steps that you need to take. And I want to emphasize also that it's not hard to do this. You have to think a little bit about what these boundary conditions should be.
cues.zh: 这就是你需要做的，对吧？这些就是你需要采取的步骤。我还想强调，做这个并不难。你只需要稍微想一下这些边界条件应该是什么。

cues.en: But this is what's required

cues.zh: 我们

cues.en: us to
cues.zh: 所需要做的，

cues.en: be able to make these robust systems, for us to be able to ride out the behavior of the outside world.
cues.zh: 才能构建这些健壮的系统，才能扛住外部世界的行为。

cues.en: And I want to make one additional point about the
cues.zh: 我还想就聊天室这个例子补充一点

cues.en: chat room example because all the other examples I've talked about has had a queue or like two queues that are there. And we have a fixed cardinality, means that we can monitor them, have graphs associated with them, basically look at them and understand their behavior very particularly.
cues.zh: 因为我讲过的其他例子都有一个队列，或者两个队列在那儿。而且基数固定，意味着我们可以监控它们，给它们配图表，基本上就是观察它们，非常具体地理解它们的行为。

cues.en: But with the chat room example, we have sort of an untold number of queues. The queues are constantly disappearing and reappearing in new configurations.
cues.zh: 但在聊天室这个例子里，我们有数不清的队列。这些队列不断地消失，又以新的配置重新出现。

cues.en: And so
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: the sort of typical monitoring thing, which is to look at all the individual queues,
cues.zh: 那种典型的监控方式，也就是查看所有单独的队列，

cues.en: is not sufficient.
cues.zh: 是不够的。

cues.en: And it becomes very hard for us to understand the system as a whole because the system is constantly changing out from underneath us.
cues.zh: 而且我们很难从整体上理解这个系统，因为系统在我们脚下不断变化。

cues.en: And so I think that this is a real problem if you think about what this would look like for core async.
cues.zh: 所以我觉得，如果你想想这在core async里会是什么样，这就是个真正的问题。

cues.en: You have all these goroutines that are sort of like shoving messages in every direction. But you can't look at it and sort of apprehend it as a whole.
cues.zh: 你有所有这些goroutine，它们像是在往各个方向塞消息。但你没法看着它、把它作为一个整体来把握。

cues.en: And I think that this is a weakness, at least for certain classes of applications.
cues.zh: 我觉得这是一个弱点，至少对某些类型的应用来说是这样。

cues.en: And so in manifold, I've played around with this a little bit. And one of the things that you can do is you can look at any stream and ask it, what streams are downstream of you? What are you feeding into?
cues.zh: 所以在manifold里，我在这方面做了一些尝试。你能做的一件事就是，你可以查看任何一个流，问它：你下游有哪些流？你在往什么里面送数据？

cues.en: And this is because all these methods, the connect method or the consume method, actually make a marker, update this sort of internal topology.
cues.zh: 这是因为所有这些方法，connect方法或consume方法，实际上都会做一个标记，更新这个内部拓扑结构。

cues.en: And this means that we can to some degree, right, trace the system, look at each of the streams, understand how they are feeding into each other.
cues.zh: 这意味着我们在某种程度上可以追踪系统，查看每个流，理解它们如何相互输入。

cues.en: It's not clear to me exactly how this should be represented. In some of my earlier attempts at this, I had, graphvis visualizations. But I've come to the conclusion that that doesn't scale very well, right? It doesn't take a very complex topology to make that sort of not well understood.
cues.zh: 我不太清楚这到底该怎么表示。在我早期的一些尝试中，我用过 graphvis 可视化。但后来我得出结论，那种方式扩展性不太好，对吧？不需要很复杂的拓扑结构，就会让人难以理解。

cues.en: And so maybe the right thing is to come up with a better visualization tool. Maybe it's to dump it to disk for examination later.
cues.zh: 所以也许正确的做法是做一个更好的可视化工具。也许是把它转储到磁盘上，供之后检查。

cues.en: I think that this is something which is a sort of rich
cues.zh: 我觉得这是一个内容相当丰富的

cues.en: topic and ripe for, sort of exploration.
cues.zh: 话题，很适合探索。

cues.en: But I think that, again, in order for Closure to become an ecosystem where we can build these sorts of systems that we don't just sort of cross our fingers and hope they don't fail, like this is necessary. We need to answer these questions. We need to have good answers for these questions.
cues.zh: 但我认为，同样地，为了让 Closure 成为一个我们能构建这类系统的生态系统，让我们不必只是祈祷它们不会失败，这是必要的。我们需要回答这些问题。我们需要为这些问题准备好答案。

cues.en: And so we talked about queues.
cues.zh: 所以我们谈了队列。

cues.en: And the things we learned are that unbounded queues aren't unbounded, right. They're bounded by memory or some other sort of fixed shared resource that will cause our system to fall over once that's succeeded.
cues.zh: 我们学到的是，无界队列并不是无界的，对吧。它们受限于内存或其他某种固定的共享资源，一旦资源耗尽，系统就会崩溃。

cues.en: And when we build an application, it should always account for what happens when it receives too much data.
cues.zh: 当我们构建应用时，应该始终考虑接收到过多数据时会发生什么。

cues.en: But where we're not at the sort of boundaries of our application, we're trying to write something which is more general or less opinionated or can be reused elsewhere,
cues.zh: 但在我们不在应用边界的地方，我们试图写一些更通用、更少主观倾向或可在别处复用的东西时，

cues.en: we should always use back pressure, right? We should always defer to someone else who knows better than us what to do.
cues.zh: 我们应该始终使用背压，对吧？我们应该始终听从那些比我们更清楚该怎么做的人。

cues.en: And we should demand metrics everywhere, right? Even if we don't actually get them, even if there are always things that are a little bit out of sight, we should always be asking for more. We should always know how we can go one step deeper.
cues.zh: 我们应该在任何地方都要求有指标，对吧？即使实际上拿不到，即使总有些东西脱离了我们的视野，我们也应该始终追求更多，始终弄清楚怎样才能更深入一层。
